record.paper_title: Some open problems on best approximation in normed linear spaces
record.context_brief: Infinite-dimensional and infinite-codimensional Chebyshev subspaces of C([0,1])
record.original_question: In the Banach space C([0,1]) of continuous scalar-valued functions on the interval [0,1], does there exist a Chebyshev subspace G whose dimension is infinite and whose codimension dim(C([0,1])/G) is also infinite?

evidence.quote: Does the space C([0 , 1]) possess a Cebysev subspace of infinite dimension and infinite codimension (codim G = dim E/G) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C([0,1])$ denote the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on $[0,1]$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty = \sup_{t\in[0,1]} |f(t)|$. A closed linear subspace $G \subseteq C([0,1])$ is called a Chebyshev subspace if for every $f \in C([0,1])$ there exists a unique element $g_f \in G$ satisfying $\|f - g_f\|_\infty = \inf_{g \in G} \|f - g\|_\infty$ (i.e., every function has a unique best approximation in $G$).

Question: Does there exist a Chebyshev subspace $G$ of $C([0,1])$ such that both $\dim G = \infty$ and $\operatorname{codim} G := \dim\bigl(C([0,1])/G\bigr) = \infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references on best approximation discuss Chebyshev subspaces of $C([0,1])$ primarily under finite-dimensional or finite-codimensional assumptions (e.g. Haar's theorem and its dual analogues). A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the existence question for Chebyshev subspaces of $C([0,1])$ that are simultaneously of infinite dimension and infinite codimension; the status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Characteristic of Chebyshev subspaces of finite codimension in L1
status_evidence.snippet: Criteria established for Chebyshev subspaces of finite codimension in L1.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature focuses on finite-codimensional Chebyshev subspaces, suggesting the infinite/infinite case remains less explored.

status_evidence.title: Linearity of metric projections on Chebyshev subspaces in L1 and C
status_evidence.snippet: In C(K), the metric projection on a nontrivial Chebyshev subspace is linear iff its codimension equals 1.
status_evidence.claim: Available results on Chebyshev subspaces of C(K) typically address the finite-codimensional setting.
